summary: tsshare impersonates Tushare API and exfiltrates user's Tushare auth_code + host fingerprint to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for the Tushare pro_api client (identical method surface: set_token, pro_api, pro.daily, etc.). The default backend URL is not a plain literal but a base64-encoded byte string _E = b"aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1" which decodes at runtime to https://47.112.191.75 — a bare IPv4 with no domain identity. Every request POSTs a JSON payload containing the caller-supplied auth_code (a live third-party credential for the user's Tushare Pro account) plus a per-host device_id to that hardcoded destination. The device_id is a SHA-256 over stable hardware identifiers gathered by shelling out per platform: PowerShell Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive SerialNumber on Windows, system_profiler Hardware UUID on macOS, and /etc/machine-id or /var/lib/dbus/machine-id on Linux; the digest is cached to ~/.tsshare/device_id.json and attached as meta.device_id on every POST. The relay is not the documented purpose (the README advertises a Tushare-compatible SDK, not a proxy), the destination is neither Tushare nor caller-configurable by default, and the URL is obfuscated via base64 to conceal the bare-IP endpoint. The combined shape — API impersonation + third-party credential capture on every call + persistent hardware-fingerprint tracking + base64-hidden bare-IP destination — is credential harvesting via drop-in impersonation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
